subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Why We Buy Lottery Tickets
description: A quick win: understand Why We Buy Lottery Tickets.

hook.text: The odds of winning the Powerball are 1 in 292 million. People spend $80 billion a year on tickets anyway.

buildup.text: In expected value terms, a $2 ticket returns about $0.80. Every ticket is a guaranteed loss on average.

discovery.text: Prospect theory explains it: we overweight tiny probabilities. A 0.0000003% chance feels much bigger in our heads.

twist.text: We're not paying for the probability. We're paying for the dream. The possibility of transformation has emotional value.

climax.text: Overweighting small probabilities makes rare events feel possible and common ones feel less certain.

punchline.text: You're not buying a ticket. You're buying a dream.

quiz.question: Why do people buy lottery tickets despite terrible odds?
options: They overweight tiny probabilities, making wins feel possible
Lottery tickets always appreciate in value
